stories.story_raw: Farmer Ramesh harvested 24 fresh ripe tomatoes from his terraced hillside plot this morning. Before setting off for the weekly village mandi, he evenly distributed them across 6 woven cane baskets so none would get bruised on the rocky pathway.

curriculum.standard: NCERT M3.04: Division as Equal Sharing
curriculum.cognitive_tier: Concrete Manipulative → Tactile Collaboration → Abstract Symbolic

digital_station.title: Interactive Tablet Scene (Shared Device Station)
digital_station.tagline: 5-8 min rotation per 10-student cohort on single rugged tablet
digital_station.instructions: Touch and drag each tomato from the harvest crate into the 6 baskets so every basket holds an equal number.
digital_station.scaffold_rule: Attempt before hint: System withholds prompts until student makes an authentic first trial.
digital_station.hint: Try placing 1 tomato into each of the 6 baskets first, then repeat until all 24 are shared.

physical_station.title: Collaborative Group Activity (Tactile Station)
physical_station.tagline: Hands-on floor task using 24 real seeds/pebbles and 6 chalk circles
materials: 6 chalk circles drawn on classroom mud floor

roles.name: Counter
roles.task: Counts total seeds aloud in local dialect

roles.name: Verifier
roles.task: Checks that each chalk circle has an identical count

physical_station.verbal_prompt: Explain aloud to your group: 'We shared 24 seeds among 6 circles, and each circle got exactly 4 seeds because 6 times 4 makes 24.'

paper_station.title: Paper & Blackboard Assessment (Evaluation Station)
paper_station.tagline: Low-cost printable transfer worksheet or copyable blackboard guide
paper_station.core_problem: Farmer Ramesh brings 24 tomatoes in 6 baskets. How many tomatoes are in each basket? (Draw or write the number)

transfer_challenge.prompt: Novel Transfer Variation: What if Farmer Ramesh harvested 30 tomatoes and brought 5 baskets instead?
transfer_challenge.pedagogical_purpose: Guarantees student masters the generalized mathematical rule (Equal Partitioning), preventing rote recall.

stories.story_raw: Master Weaver Meera gathered 18 seasoned bamboo splints to weave a traditional grain storage lid. She arranged them into 3 symmetrical chevron triangles to balance the tension across the bamboo rim.

curriculum.cognitive_tier: Tactile Splints → Visual Angles → Abstract Ratios

digital_station.title: Interactive Tablet Scene (Shared Device Station)
digital_station.tagline: 5-8 min rotation per 10-student cohort on single rugged tablet
digital_station.instructions: Place 18 bamboo splints evenly into 3 triangular frames to complete the symmetrical weaving pattern.
digital_station.scaffold_rule: Attempt before hint: System withholds prompts until student makes an authentic first trial.
digital_station.hint: Count how many splints fit into one triangle before moving to the next.

physical_station.title: Collaborative Group Activity (Tactile Station)
physical_station.tagline: Hands-on floor task using 18 twigs/splints and 3 chalk triangles

roles.name: Angle Inspector
roles.task: Checks that each triangle has 6 sticks

roles.name: Spokesperson
roles.task: Articulates the symmetry ratio to the class

physical_station.verbal_prompt: Explain: '18 bamboo splints split among 3 equal triangles gives 6 per triangle because 3 × 6 = 18.'

paper_station.title: Paper & Blackboard Assessment (Evaluation Station)
paper_station.tagline: Low-cost printable transfer worksheet or copyable blackboard guide
paper_station.core_problem: Artisan Meera needs 18 bamboo sticks for 3 baskets. How many sticks go into each basket?

transfer_challenge.prompt: Novel Transfer Variation: What if she had 24 sticks and 4 baskets? How many sticks per basket?
transfer_challenge.pedagogical_purpose: Validates that student generalizes division to multiple spatial contexts.

stories.story_raw: Elder Sonam brought 40 kilograms of winter potatoes to the valley cooperative market. The cooperative manager packed them into 4 identical jute sacks to transport on the pack ponies.

curriculum.standard: NCERT M3.08: Units of Weight & Division
curriculum.cognitive_tier: Scale Manipulatives → Jute Sacks → Numeric Units

digital_station.title: Interactive Tablet Scene (Shared Device Station)
digital_station.tagline: 5-8 min rotation per 10-student cohort on single rugged tablet
digital_station.instructions: Distribute 40 kg of potatoes equally into the 4 jute sacks.
digital_station.scaffold_rule: Attempt before hint: System withholds prompts until student makes an authentic first trial.
digital_station.hint: Think of tens: how many tens make forty?

physical_station.title: Collaborative Group Activity (Tactile Station)
physical_station.tagline: Hands-on floor task using clay weights and 4 sack outlines
physical_station.verbal_prompt: Explain: '40 kg divided into 4 sacks equals 10 kg each because 4 × 10 = 40.'

paper_station.title: Paper & Blackboard Assessment (Evaluation Station)
paper_station.tagline: Low-cost printable transfer worksheet or copyable blackboard guide
paper_station.core_problem: Elder Sonam packs 40 kg of potatoes in 4 sacks. How many kg in each sack?

transfer_challenge.prompt: Novel Transfer Variation: What if the harvest was 45 kg across 5 sacks?
transfer_challenge.pedagogical_purpose: Tests flexible mental division with multiples of five.
